Reasoning: The problem states that ρ_i is the intrinsic resistivity of silicon. For an intrinsic semiconductor, ρ_i approximately satisfies ρ_i ∝ exp(E_g/(2k_B T)); taking the natural logarithm of both sides gives ln(ρ_i) ≈ C + (E_g/(2k_B))(1/T). Therefore, in the approximately straight-line graph of ln(ρ_i) versus 1/T, the slope is approximately E_g/(2k_B), which can be used to estimate the band gap energy E_g of silicon.

method.method_draft: Classify the displayed graph as an Arrhenius plot because the y-axis is ln(rho_i) and the x-axis is 1/T. Use the text to identify the material as intrinsic silicon. Recall that intrinsic conduction is thermally activated across the energy gap; resistivity decreases as carriers are thermally generated. Thus the activation energy encoded in the slope corresponds to half the band-gap energy, so the slope can be converted to the band gap energy of silicon, E_g.
